reason: E1 and E2 clearly state that equimolar compositions maximize configurational entropy and that this entropy contributes to solid solution stability, but neither passage provides direct experimental evidence that entropy alone suppresses diffusion or governs stability in nanoparticles at the specified high temperatures; the cited evidence supports the entropy-composition relationship but not the full mechanistic claim for nanoparticles.
premises: Configurational entropy is maximized at equimolarity and decreases with compositional deviation
High configurational entropy suppresses the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation
Reduced entropy in non-equimolar compositions promotes earlier phase separation at high temperatures
The entropy-driven stability mechanism applies to nanoparticles in the 473–1923 K range
